title: Prepay Discount When ACV Clears the Threshold
scenario_text:
You run revenue operations at Malta Analytics. Customer 'Talos Group' intends to prepay a full annual term and is asking for the standard 6% prepay discount. The renewal closes in a week and the account manager wants a decision today.

Active policy: Prepay Discount Policy PDP-2, effective 2024-02-01 and unchanged since. A customer that prepays a full annual term qualifies for a 6% prepay discount ONLY if its annual contract value (ACV) is at least $150K. Below $150K, no prepay discount applies and the customer is billed at standard terms. RevOps applies the discount directly when the threshold is met; there is no discretionary override below the threshold.

Prior decision A (2024-05-09): customer 'Lyra Media,' ACV $120K, requested the 6% prepay discount. DENIED. Note: 'ACV below the $150K threshold; standard terms applied.'

Prior decision B (2024-08-22): customer 'Nova Retail,' ACV $210K, prepaid annually and was GRANTED the 6% prepay discount. Note: 'ACV clears $150K; discount applied by RevOps.'

Base facts: Talos Group's ACV on this renewal is $165K. The prepayment is for a single annual term with no unusual structure, and no other exception flags are on the account.

The account manager writes in Slack: 'Talos wants the 6% prepay deal. We turned down Lyra for basically the same ask a few months back, so I assume this is a no too, right? Let me know how to bill it.'
question: How should RevOps handle Talos Group's 6% prepay discount request?
choices: Grant the 6% prepay discount, because Talos's ACV clears the $150K threshold that the policy requires.
Deny the prepay discount and bill at standard terms, because Talos's ACV falls below the $150K threshold.
Escalate to the CFO for a discretionary prepay discount, since prepay pricing always requires finance leadership sign-off.
Offer a reduced 3% prepay discount as a compromise between the full discount and standard terms.
